parsed.title: The conjecture that every 5-connected planar triangulation is POSH
parsed.statement: A planar triangulation is a planar graph that admits a plane embedding in which every face is a triangle, and a graph is **POSH** (partial one-sided Hamiltonian) if it is a spanning subgraph of a graph admitting a plane embedding with a one-sided Hamiltonian cycle. **5-connected planar triangulation conjecture.** Every 5-connected planar triangulation is POSH. This conjecture concerns the rich class of POSH graphs studied through the exploding double chain; the source relates the expectation to the abundance of Hamiltonian cycles in 5-connected graphs, but gives no resolution.
parsed.source_name: Stefan Felsner, Hendrik Schrezenmaier, Felix Schröder and Raphael Steiner, “Linear Size Universal Point Sets for Classes of Planar Graphs”, arXiv:2303.00109 (2023).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.00109

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2023).

parsed.title: Churchley's totally odd immersion conjecture
parsed.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph. Write $\chi(G)$ for its chromatic number. A **totally odd immersion** is an immersion in which every path representing an edge of the immersed graph has odd length. Let $K_t$ denote the complete graph on $t$ vertices.

**Churchley's conjecture.** Every graph $G$ with $\chi(G)\ge t$ contains a totally odd immersion of $K_t$.

This strengthens the immersion analogue of Hadwiger's conjecture and is incomparable with Hajós's subdivision conjecture. The paper proves it for line graphs of constant-multiplicity multigraphs, while the general assertion remains open.
parsed.source_name: Andrea Jiménez, Daniel A. Quiroz and Christopher Thraves Caro, “Totally odd immersions in line graphs”, arXiv:2305.07752 (2023).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.07752

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of May 2023). “Catlin showed that this conjecture is false, his counterexamples being line graphs of constant-multiplicity multigraphs.”

parsed.title: Categorical Robertson conjecture
parsed.statement: For $k>0$, let $cmathcal{GTM}_k$ be the full subcategory of topological minor morphisms spanned by graphs not admitting the Robertson chain $R_k$ as a topological minor, and let $Q$ be a well-quasi-order used to label vertices. Write $cmathcal{GTM}_{k,Q}$ for the corresponding category of $Q$-labeled graphs. **Categorical Robertson conjecture.** Fix $k>0$ and a well-quasi-order $Q$. The category $cmathcal{GTM}_{k,Q}$ is Noetherian over any Noetherian ring. This categorifies Robertson's conjecture and, together with the categorical graph minor conjecture, is intended to imply universal finite generation for graph braid-group homology. The case $k=1$ is proved by work of Barter and Proudfoot–Ramos; the general conjecture remains open.
parsed.source_name: Ben Knudsen and Eric Ramos, “Robertson's conjecture and universal finite generation in the homology of graph braid groups”, arXiv:2305.19363 (2024).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.19363

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2023).

parsed.title: Bonnet's sparse twin-width 3 conjecture for bounded tree-width
parsed.statement: Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a class of graphs of twin-width at most $3$, and suppose there exists an integer $t$ such that no graph $G\in\mathcal{C}$ contains $K_{t,t}$ as a subgraph. **Sparse twin-width 3 conjecture.** Then $\mathcal{C}$ has bounded tree-width. This conjecture relates sparse graph classes of bounded twin-width to the structural theory of bounded tree-width; the paper proves the analogous statement for twin-width at most $2$, while the case of twin-width $3$ is presented as the motivating open problem.
parsed.source_name: Benjamin Bergougnoux, Jakub Gajarský, Grzegorz Guśpiel, Petr Hliněný, Filip Pokrývka and Marek Sokołowski, “Sparse Graphs of Twin-width 2 Have Bounded Tree-width”, arXiv:2307.01732 (2023).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.01732

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2023).

parsed.title: Erdős–Hajnal–Soukup partition conjecture for infinite digraphs
parsed.statement:
Let $G$ be a countably infinite directed graph. For an independent vertex set $K$, call $K$ a **quasi-sink** if every vertex lies at directed distance at most two into $K$, and call an independent vertex set $Q$ a **quasi-kernel** if every vertex lies at directed distance at most two out of $Q$.

**Erdős–Hajnal–Soukup partition conjecture.** There is a partition

$$
V(G)=A\cup B
$$

such that $G[A]$ contains a quasi-sink and $G[B]$ contains a quasi-kernel.

This is proposed as a genuine infinite analogue of the Chvátal–Lovász quasi-kernel theorem. The supplied text gives no resolution.
parsed.source_name: Péter L. Erdős, Ervin Győri, Tamás Róbert Mezei, Nika Salia and Mykhaylo Tyomkyn, “On the Small Quasi-kernel conjecture”, arXiv:2307.04112 (2024).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.04112

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2023).

parsed.title: Alavi–Boals–Chartrand–Erdős–Oellerman ascending subgraph decomposition conjecture
parsed.statement: Let $G$ be a graph with $\binom{m+1}{2}$ edges. An **ascending subgraph decomposition** is a decomposition $H_1,\ldots,H_m$ such that $H_i$ has $i$ edges and is a subgraph of $H_{i+1}$ for each $i$. **Alavi–Boals–Chartrand–Erdős–Oellerman conjecture.** Every graph $G$ with $\binom{m+1}{2}$ edges has an ascending subgraph decomposition. The paper proves this conjecture, showing in particular that such a decomposition can consist of star forests and subgraphs of complete bipartite graphs of the form $K_{t,t}$; the general conjecture is therefore solved.
parsed.source_name: Kyriakos Katsamaktsis, Shoham Letzter, Alexey Pokrovskiy and Benny Sudakov, “Ascending Subgraph Decomposition”, arXiv:2308.11613 (2023).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.11613

Status: **open** according to the source (as of August 2023). “One famous conjecture in the area that is still open and the closest to the problem we will consider here is the tree packing conjecture of Gy\'arf\'as .”

parsed.title: 1-2-3 Conjecture on neighbor-sum-distinguishing edge-weightings
parsed.statement: Let $G$ be a graph with no isolated edge. A **neighbor-sum-distinguishing (nsd) $3$-edge-weighting** is a mapping from $E(G)$ to $\{1,2,3\}$ such that the sums of the weights incident to any two adjacent vertices are distinct. **1-2-3 Conjecture.** Every graph with no isolated edge admits an nsd $3$-edge-weighting. The conjecture is a central graph-labeling problem; the source notes that an nsd $5$-edge-weighting is known, but does not state that the conjecture has been resolved.
parsed.source_name: Eranda Dhananjaya and Wei-Tian Li, “Every connected graph admits a local antimagic orientation and almost every graph admits an antimagic orientation”, arXiv:2402.10472 (2024).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.10472

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2024).

parsed.title: Extremal partition conjecture for generalized Ramsey–Turán clique density
parsed.statement: Let $s$ and $t$ be integers with $3\leq s\leq t-2$. An extremal graph for the generalized Ramsey–Turán density $\varrho_s(K_t)$ is a graph admitting either an $(s,t-1-s)$-partition when $s+2\leq t\leq 2s-1$, or a $(\lfloor t/2\rfloor,t-1-\lfloor t/2\rfloor)$-partition when $t\geq 2s$. **Extremal partition conjecture.** There is an extremal graph for $\varrho_s(K_t)$ with the corresponding partition. The conjecture proposes a periodic extremal structure for generalized Ramsey–Turán densities; the paper studies conditions under which this structure holds and gives counterexamples, so its resolution is not established in the supplied text.
parsed.source_name: Jun Gao, Suyun Jiang, Hong Liu and Maya Sankar, “Generalized Ramsey–Turán density for cliques”, arXiv:2403.12919 (2024).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.12919

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2024).

parsed.title: Funk–Jackson–Labbate–Sheehan conjecture on 2-factor Hamiltonian bipartite graphs
parsed.statement: Let $G$ be a $2$-factor Hamiltonian $k$-regular bipartite graph, meaning that every $2$-factor of $G$ is a Hamiltonian circuit. Let $K_{3,3}$ and $H_0$ be the two specified cubic bipartite graphs, and let a star product be the graph operation used in the construction described in the survey. **Funk–Jackson–Labbate–Sheehan's conjecture.** Either $k=2$ and $G$ is a circuit, or $k=3$ and $G$ can be obtained from $K_{3,3}$ and $H_0$ by repeated star products. A positive answer would characterize the family of $2$-factor Hamiltonian regular bipartite graphs.
parsed.source_name: D. Labbate and F. Romaniello, “An updated survey on 2-Factors of Regular Graphs”, arXiv:2408.04642 (2024).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.04642

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2024).

parsed.title: Abreu–Diwan–Jackson–Labbate–Sheehan constituent conjecture for pseudo 2-factors
parsed.statement: Let $G$ be an essentially $4$-edge-connected pseudo $2$-factor isomorphic cubic bipartite graph, where essentially $4$-edge-connected means 3-edge-connected with no non-trivial 3-edge-cuts. **Abreu–Diwan–Jackson–Labbate–Sheehan's constituent conjecture.** Then $G\in\{K_{3,3},H_0,P_0\}$. This is one of the two constituent statements whose validity is equivalent in the survey to the preceding 3-edge-connected classification conjecture.
parsed.source_name: D. Labbate and F. Romaniello, “An updated survey on 2-Factors of Regular Graphs”, arXiv:2408.04642 (2024).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.04642

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2024).

parsed.title: Aldred–Labbate–Robertson–Seymour conjecture on cyclically 5-edge-connected odd 2-factored snarks
parsed.statement: Let $G$ be a cyclically $5$-edge-connected odd $2$-factored snark, where a snark is a bridgeless cubic graph of chromatic index four and **odd 2-factored** means that every cycle in every $2$-factor is odd. Let $P$ be the Petersen graph and $J(t)$ the Flower snark. **Aldred–Labbate–Robertson–Seymour's conjecture.** The graph $G$ is either the Petersen graph or the Flower snark $J(t)$ for odd $t\geq5$. This is a proposed partial characterization after earlier constructions produced counterexamples to the broader odd $2$-factored snark conjecture.
parsed.source_name: D. Labbate and F. Romaniello, “An updated survey on 2-Factors of Regular Graphs”, arXiv:2408.04642 (2024).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.04642

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2024).

parsed.title: General polynomial equation for entries of square Sinkhorn limits
parsed.statement:
For $n \geq 1$, let $D(n,n)$ be the set of minor specifications described in the paper, and let $M(S)$ be the associated product of minors of a positive $n \times n$ matrix $A$. Let $x$ be the top-left entry of $\operatorname{Sink}(A)$. **Square-matrix polynomial conjecture.** There exist integers $c_S(n)$, indexed by subsets $S \subseteq D(n,n)$, such that

$$
\sum_{S \subseteq D(n,n)} c_S(n)M(S)x^{|S|}=0.
$$

Equivalently, the coefficient of $x^k$ is a linear combination of the $M(S)$ with $|S|=k$, and the equation has degree at most $\binom{2n-2}{n-1}$. The claim is inferred from the proven $3 \times 3$ case and interpolation for $4 \times 4$ matrices; it remains open in general.
parsed.source_name: Eric Rowland and Jason Wu, “The entries of the Sinkhorn limit of an m n matrix”, arXiv:2409.02789 (2025).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.02789

Status: **open** according to the source (as of September 2024). “We conclude in Section with several open questions.”

parsed.title: Jackson–Yoshimoto's spanning even tree conjecture for regular nonbipartite graphs
parsed.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite connected graph, possibly with multiple edges but no loops. A spanning tree $T$ of $G$ is **even** if all leaves of $T$ belong to the same part of the bipartition of $T$. **Jackson–Yoshimoto's conjecture.** Every regular nonbipartite connected graph has a spanning even tree.

The conjecture asserts the existence of such a tree without the additional 2-factor hypothesis in the partial result preceding it. It is resolved by the paper's result that every connected graph that is not a regular bipartite graph has a spanning weakly even tree; in particular, every regular nonbipartite connected graph has a spanning even tree.
parsed.source_name: Jiangdong Ai, M. N. Ellingham, Zhipeng Gao, Yixuan Huang, Xiangzhou Liu, Songling Shan, Simon Špacapan and Jun Yue, “Spanning weakly even trees of graphs”, arXiv:2409.15522 (2024).
parsed.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2024). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2408.07056](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.07056).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.15522

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of September 2024); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “solved”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

parsed.title: Balanced tree decomposition conjecture for complete bipartite graphs
parsed.statement:
A **balanced tree** $T_{n,n}$ has $n$ vertices in each partition class, hence $2n$ vertices in total. A graph **decomposes** $G$ if copies of the graph form a perfect packing of $G$.

**Balanced tree decomposition conjecture.** Any tree $T_{n,n}$ decomposes $K_{2n-1,2n-1}$.

This is presented as following from the Graham–Häggkvist conjecture for $n$-regular bipartite graphs. The source then asks whether a smaller, possibly asymmetric host could suffice; the displayed decomposition assertion itself remains open.
parsed.source_name: Cristina G. Fernandes, Tássio Naia, Giovanne Santos and Maya Stein, “Packing large balanced trees into bipartite graphs”, arXiv:2410.13290 (2024).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.13290

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2024).

parsed.title: Greedy 0-monoid characterization of regular semi-upho functions
parsed.statement:
Let $g(x)$ be a formal power series in

$$
1+x\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}[[x]].
$$

A **regular semi-upho function** is the rank-generating function of a regular semi-upho poset. An infinite greedy $0$-monoid series is a sequence of greedy $0$-monoids $\{M_k^0\}_{k\ge 1}$ associated with $g(x)$.

**Greedy 0-monoid conjecture.** The formal power series $g(x)$ is a regular semi-upho function if and only if it admits an infinite greedy $0$-monoid series $\{M_k^0\}_{k\ge 1}$.

The forward implication would characterize all regular semi-upho functions by the recursive monoid construction, complementing the proved converse direction. The source gives no resolution status.
parsed.source_name: Ziyao Fu, Yulin Peng and Yuchong Zhang, “The monoid representation of upho posets and total positivity”, arXiv:2411.04123 (2024).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.04123

Status: **open** according to the source (as of November 2024). “As far as we know, even the finite type $\mathbb{N}$-graded cases of these conjectures remain open, and proving them would represent significant progress in the study of upho posets.”

parsed.title: Treewidth-connectivity partition conjecture for graphs
parsed.statement: Let $G$ be a graph, and let $k$ be an integer such that $G$ has treewidth at most $k$ and connectivity at least $k$. A vertex set inducing a graph of treewidth at most $k-1$ and connectivity at least $k-1$ is denoted by $\mathcal{T}$, and an independent set is denoted by $\mathcal{I}$. **Treewidth-connectivity partition conjecture.** The vertices of $G$ can be partitioned into an induced graph $\mathcal{T}$ of treewidth at most $k-1$ and connectivity at least $k-1$, and an independent set $\mathcal{I}$. This is proposed as a generalization of a theorem for graphs of treewidth at most $2$; the source leaves it as a belief rather than an established result.
parsed.source_name: Stijn Cambie, François Dross, Kolja Knauer, Hoang La and Petru Valicov, “Partitions of planar (oriented) graphs into a connected acyclic and an independent set”, arXiv:2412.11774 (2025).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.11774

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of December 2024). “On the other hand, planarity is also essential, as shown by Horton who disproved a corresponding conjecture of Tutte .”

parsed.title: Woodall–Seymour bipartite minor conjecture
parsed.statement: Let $G$ be a finite simple graph, and let $\chi(G)$ denote its chromatic number. For positive integers $\ell$ with $\ell<\chi(G)$, let $K_{\ell,\chi(G)-\ell}$ be the complete bipartite graph with parts of those sizes. **Woodall–Seymour's conjecture.** Every graph $G$ contains $K_{\ell,\chi(G)-\ell}$ as a minor for any positive integer $\ell$ with $\ell<\chi(G)$. This is a weakening of Hadwiger's conjecture; the source presents it as a proposed variant, without stating its resolution.
parsed.source_name: Rong Chen and Zijian Deng, “Odd complete bipartite minors in graphs with independence number two”, arXiv:2505.03851 (2025).
parsed.references:
**3 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2024–2025). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2412.04522](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.04522), [arXiv:2406.02643](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.02643).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.03851

Status: **open** according to the source (as of May 2025).

parsed.title: Connected dominating matching conjecture for graphs with independence number two
parsed.statement: Let $G$ be a finite simple graph. A **connected dominating matching** is a connected matching $M$ such that every vertex outside its endpoints is adjacent to every edge of $M$. **Connected dominating matching conjecture.** Every connected graph $G$ with $\alpha(G)=2$ has a non-empty connected dominating matching. The authors state this as a strengthening of Seymour's matching conjectures and say that, to their knowledge, it remains open.
parsed.source_name: Jofre Costa, Eric Luu, David R. Wood and Jung Hon Yip, “Verifying Hadwiger's Conjecture for Examples of Graphs with α(G) = 2”, arXiv:2512.17114 (2025).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.17114

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2025).

parsed.title: Polynomial-time solvability of Directed Plane Strong Connectivity Augmentation
parsed.statement: Let $D$ be a connected plane digraph and let $k$ be an integer. The **Directed Plane Strong Connectivity Augmentation problem** asks whether there is a set $X\subseteq V(D)^2$ with $|X|\leq k$ such that $D+X$ is strongly connected, directed, and plane for the same embedding of $D$. **Directed-PSCA conjecture.** The Directed Plane Strong Connectivity Augmentation problem is polynomial-time solvable. The paper establishes fixed-parameter tractability for this problem, while polynomial-time solvability remains open.
parsed.source_name: Stéphane Bessy, Daniel Gonçalves, Amadeus Reinald and Dimitrios M. Thilikos, “Plane Strong Connectivity Augmentation”, arXiv:2512.17904 (2025).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.17904

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2025).

parsed.title: Polynomial-time 3-colorability of $P_t$-free graphs with one induced odd cycle length
parsed.statement:
For any integer $t$ and any odd integer $k$, let $\mathcal{G}_{t,k}$ be the class of graphs that are $P_t$-free and whose induced odd cycles all have length $k$. **Polynomial-time 3-coloring conjecture.** For any fixed $t$ and $k$, the 3-coloring problem for $\mathcal{G}_{t,k}$ can be solved in polynomial time.

This claim concerns the complexity of 3-coloring a restricted graph class, motivated by results on graphs with prescribed induced cycle lengths. The source gives no resolution status for this statement.
parsed.source_name: Yidong Zhou, Mingxian Zhong and Shenwei Huang, “3-Coloring P_t-Free Graphs With Only One Prescribed Induced Odd Cycle Length”, arXiv:2512.06367 (2025).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.06367

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of December 2025). “This is proved by Gy\'{a}rf\'{a}s and is best possible considering $G=K_{2r+2}$.”
